sayLines.line: Filled 1L (clean — Haven well). 3L carried (3kg). (-10 kcal hauling, 1 tick.) Cistern: 24L left.
"You haven't earned that yet," A person, maybe 20s says. (Trust too low.)

Travel 1 tile to meadow.
— Open ground —
Open sky for the first time in a while. Hawks circle — something down there is being watched.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to grove.
— Nut trees —
Hickories and oaks, heavy with mast. This is a pantry that grows.
Movement — a long gray snake coiled on a sunlit log.
👁 No rattle, no venom — but your hands don't know that yet. It freezes, hoping you'll walk past. Pin it behind the head; it bites only when grabbed.
Unfamiliar unknown shoots — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Journal: Riparian ground. Water means life, and lunch.
The System notes the synergy — foraged a plant new to this ground: +1 field XP.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND Green Thumb, Literally. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.
A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 5× unknown shoots. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.

Travel 2 tiles to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Saplings push up through last year's deadfall, racing each other for the light. The forest never stops trying.
Something moves out there — a boulder with opinions about where you're walking.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.
📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
You've learned Old World Caches — it carries Eagle Eye.

Travel 2 tiles to ruin.
— Pre-Burn ruin —
A collapsed barn. Pre-Burn. The wiring is gone — everything is gone — but the stones remember the shape of work.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND Scrounger. It resonates with: something unnamed.
You pry open a cupboard: Trail Rations Pouch. A waxed pouch, still buckled, the kind a careful walker packs the night before.
Travel 1 tile to Haven.
It stops at the treeline — pacing, unwilling. The walls end the argument. Something heavy rooting in the grass is still out there.
You keep a day's food (1400 kcal) — nothing extra for the pantry this time.
1 unprocessed haul onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
You walk back into Haven. 1 Codex entry. The village is glad to see you.
📋 A woman, maybe 60s wants to know what's by the creek. "Just look. Come back and tell me."
A person, maybe 20s heads out for water. "Fetching water. Somebody has to." The pantry won't fill itself.
A person, maybe 40s heads out for water. "Off to the well — back with a full skin." The pantry won't fill itself.
A man, maybe 30s heads out for water. "Thirst doesn't negotiate. Going." The pantry won't fill itself.
A woman, maybe 30s heads out for water. "The well won't fill itself." The pantry won't fill itself.

A man, maybe 40s heads out for water. "Fetching water. Somebody has to." The pantry won't fill itself.
Cormac is staying at Haven as the camp healer now — tending the sick instead of ranging out.
Iron cold. Even the ticks are shelved.
— MIDDAY — Honest work hours. Heat builds.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
You eat Dried meat (600 kcal).
"You haven't earned that yet," A person, maybe 20s says. (Trust too low.)

— DUSK — Animals stir again. Shadows lengthen.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
A person, maybe 20s shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)
— NIGHT — Camp. Rest — or risk the dark.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
You wait. The light changes. Nothing asks anything of you.
A man, maybe 40s picks through the bag, frowning. Nothing they can name with confidence. (8 ticks)
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You catch fragments by the fire — A woman, maybe 40s, with a wiry build telling A person, maybe 50s, with a slouched posture about A person, maybe 20s. The retelling is already better than the event.

💧 A woman, maybe 30s returns with water: +2 clean.

"Hey." A person, maybe 50s, with a slouched posture settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A person, maybe 50s, with a slouched posture.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A woman, maybe 40s, with sun-creased eyes came back with an armful of something edible, unprompted. (+100 kcal pantry)

A person, maybe 50s, with a slouched posture spends the afternoon with the tall plumes of small yellow flowers in fall, narrow leaves — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. By evening a person, maybe 50s, with a slouched posture is thoroughly, educationally sick. "NOT food," they announce to the fire, pale. "My body told me so." The lesson is learned the hard way — and now the whole village knows it.
From the lumped bag: Goldenrod — named, and out.
★ IDENTIFIED: Goldenrod. Tall yellow flower plumes in fall. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
💡 The tall plumes of small yellow flowers in fall, narrow leaves — THAT's what A person, maybe 50s, with a slouched posture was describing. Goldenrod. It clicks like a key turning.
A woman, maybe 60s was watching. Now they know Goldenrod too.
The Journal notes it: Goldenrod — NOT food. (A person, maybe 50s, with a slouched posture tested it.)
